scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kikkli, also spelled Kikli, is an Indian folk dance performed by Punjabi women and young girls.
It functions as both a folk dance tradition and a competitive physical sport among youth.
on_screen: Map: India · South Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Kikkli combines dance and sport.
It provides physical activity, balance training, and social enjoyment for young Punjabi girls during informal community gatherings.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Two girls stand face to face close together, cross their arms, and interlock their hands firmly.
Leaning their bodies backward so their arms stretch to the maximum, they use this counter balance to wheel round rapidly in continuous circular motions.
It is performed primarily in pairs, though sometimes four girls execute the dance together.
Watch for Interlocked Twirl.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (OvC4_lwKFSY)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Small stationary circular footprint, twirling in place in pairs or groups of four.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is accompanied by folk songs and rhythmic clapping.
The surrounding audience of women sings folk tunes and claps, encouraging the twirling pair to increase their speed continuously.
Listen for the clapping.
Vocal folk singing accompanied by hand clapping and the continuous tinkling of dancers' anklets as they spin.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear traditional clothing with floating dupattas (scarves) and anklets.
As the girls spin, their dupattas float outward in the air and their anklets produce a rhythmic tinkling sound.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Stand face-to-face close to a partner.
Step 2: Cross arms and interlock hands firmly with the partner.
Footwork from the sources: Wheeling rapidly and continuously in small circular paths while maintaining counter-balanced weight.
Drill: Practice crossing arms and locking hands with a partner.

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Incline body backward until arms are stretched to maximum length.
Step 4: Wheel round continuously in rapid circular motions while maintaining balance.
Drill: Practice leaning backward in a static position to test mutual counterweight.
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
